claim: TRPM3 is activated by pregnenolone sulfate.

claim: TRPM3 is a well-established temperature sensor in peripheral sensory neurons of the dorsal root ganglia.
source: TRPM3 is a well-established temperature sensor in peripheral sensory neurons of the dorsal root ganglia (DRG); its genetic deletion in mice leads to defects in noxious heat sensation as well as reduced inflammatory heat hyperalgesia (Vriens et al., 2011; Vandewauw et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vriens et al., 2011 and Vandewauw et al., 2018

claim: Genetic deletion of TRPM3 in mice leads to defects in noxious heat sensation.
source: TRPM3 is a well-established temperature sensor in peripheral sensory neurons of the dorsal root ganglia (DRG); its genetic deletion in mice leads to defects in noxious heat sensation as well as reduced inflammatory heat hyperalgesia (Vriens et al., 2011; Vandewauw et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vriens et al., 2011 and Vandewauw et al., 2018

claim: Genetic deletion of TRPM3 in mice leads to reduced inflammatory heat hyperalgesia.

claim: Inhibitors of TRPM3 reduced both acute heat sensation and inflammatory heat hyperalgesia.

claim: TRPM3 shows increased activity when temperature is increased from 15°C to 26°C.

claim: TRPM3 shows further increases in activity at 37°C.

claim: The S4-S5 linker plays essential roles in channel gating.
source: The S4-S5 linker plays essential roles in channel gating, and has been shown to be a hotspot of disease-associated gain-of-function mutations in a number of TRP channels, including TRPV3, TRPV4, TRPM4 and TRPA1 (Hofmann et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hofmann et al., 2017

evidence: Supported by citation to Hofmann et al., 2017

claim: The S4-S5 linker plays a role in binding of hydrophobic or amphipathic ligands in TRPM channels.
source: This channel segment also plays a role in binding of hydrophobic, or amphipathic ligands in TRPM channels (Huang et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Huang et al., 2020

claim: In TRPM8 channels, the S4-S5 linker is in direct contact with both the cooling agent icilin and the menthol analog WS12.
source: For example, in TRPM8 channels the S4-S5 linker is in direct contact with both the cooling agent icilin, and the menthol analog WS12 (Yin et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yin et al., 2019

claim: PregS is thought to activate TRPM3 by directly binding to the channel.
source: While PregS is thought to activate TRPM3 by directly binding to the channel (Drews et al., 2014), its binding site in the channel is not known, and currently there is no structural information available for TRPM3.
evidence: Supported by citation to Drews et al., 2014

claim: The binding site of PregS in TRPM3 is not known.

claim: It is likely that the V990/992M mutation primarily increased the stability of the open state.
source: Because of the clear increase in basal activity of the V990/992M mutant, it is quite likely that the mutation primarily increased the stability of the open state and the decrease in EC50 of agonist activation is a consequence of the change in activation equilibrium constant (Colquhoun, 1998).
evidence: Inference from the observed increase in basal activity, supported by citation to Colquhoun, 1998

claim: The decrease in EC50 of agonist activation for V990/992M is a consequence of the change in activation equilibrium constant.
source: Because of the clear increase in basal activity of the V990/992M mutant, it is quite likely that the mutation primarily increased the stability of the open state and the decrease in EC50 of agonist activation is a consequence of the change in activation equilibrium constant (Colquhoun, 1998).
evidence: Inference based on thermodynamic principles, supported by citation to Colquhoun, 1998

claim: It cannot be excluded that the V990/992M mutation also affected PregS binding concurrently.
source: It cannot be excluded, however, that the mutation also affected PregS binding concurrently, given the general role of this segment in ligand binding in TRP channels.
evidence: Speculation based on the known role of the S4-S5 linker in ligand binding

claim: The membrane phospholipid phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) is required for PregS-induced TRPM3 activity.
source: The membrane phospholipid phosphatidylinositol 4,5-bisphosphate (PIP2) is also required for PregS-induced TRPM3 activity (Badheka et al., 2015; Tóth et al., 2015; Uchida et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to Badheka et al., 2015; Tóth et al., 2015; Uchida et al., 2016

claim: In TRPM8, the equivalent of V990 is two positions upstream from a residue that is in close contact with PIP2.
source: In TRPM8, the equivalent of V990 is two positions upstream from a residue that is in close contact with PIP2, and it is 4 and 7 positions downstream from two residues in close contact with icilin and the menthol analog WS12 (Yin et al., 2019; Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Supported by citation to Yin et al., 2019 and Figure 1—figure supplement 1A

claim: PIP2 is located adjacent to the menthol analogue WS12 and the cooling agent icilin in the TRPM8 structures.
source: PIP2 is located adjacent to the menthol analogue WS12 and the cooling agent icilin in the TRPM8 structures, and menthol has been shown to allosterically affect PIP2 activation (Rohács et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rohács et al., 2005

claim: Menthol has been shown to allosterically affect PIP2 activation of TRPM8.
source: PIP2 is located adjacent to the menthol analogue WS12 and the cooling agent icilin in the TRPM8 structures, and menthol has been shown to allosterically affect PIP2 activation (Rohács et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to Rohács et al., 2005

claim: It is possible that the V990/992M mutation affects PregS activation indirectly via PIP2.
source: Therefore, it is also possible that the V990/992M mutation affects PregS activation indirectly via PIP2.
evidence: Speculation based on the proximity of V990 to PIP2 binding sites in TRPM8

claim: Increased Ca2+ levels in cells expressing mutated channels may modify cellular PI(4,5)P2 levels, which may alter channel activity.
source: Increased Ca2+ levels in cells expressing mutated channels may also modify cellular PI(4,5)P2 levels, which may alter channel activity.
evidence: Speculation about potential indirect effects

claim: Large-scale unbiased mutagenesis studies on TRPV1 and TRPV3 show that mutations in the pore region and the outer portion of S6 selectively abolished heat-, but not agonist-induced channel activation.
source: While the mechanism of temperature activation of TRP channels is not fully understood (Clapham and Miller, 2011; Islas, 2017; Arrigoni and Minor, 2018; Castillo et al., 2018), large-scale unbiased mutagenesis studies on TRPV1 (Grandl et al., 2010) and TRPV3 (Grandl et al., 2008) show that mutations in the pore region and the outer portion of S6 in these channels selectively abolished heat-, but not agonist-induced channel activation.
evidence: Supported by citations to Grandl et al., 2010 and Grandl et al., 2008

claim: The P1090/1092Q mutation is located in the outer portion of S6.
source: The P1090/1092Q mutation in TRPM3 is located in the outer portion of S6, and it had a stronger effect on heat activation than the V990/992M mutation, therefore it is possible that the primary effect of the P1090/1092Q mutation is increasing heat sensitivity.
evidence: Structural information from Figure 1—figure supplement 1

claim: It is possible that the primary effect of the P1090/1092Q mutation is increasing heat sensitivity.
source: The P1090/1092Q mutation in TRPM3 is located in the outer portion of S6, and it had a stronger effect on heat activation than the V990/992M mutation, therefore it is possible that the primary effect of the P1090/1092Q mutation is increasing heat sensitivity.
evidence: Inference from the location of the mutation and its stronger effect on heat activation

claim: Increased temperatures synergize with PregS in activating wild-type TRPM3.
source: Increased temperatures synergize with PregS in activating wild-type TRPM3 (Vriens et al., 2011), see also Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, therefore it is possible that the increased PregS sensitivity of the P1090/1090Q mutant is secondary to its increased heat activation.
evidence: Supported by citation to Vriens et al., 2011 and Figure 1—figure supplement 3B

claim: It is possible that the increased PregS sensitivity of the P1090/1090Q mutant is secondary to its increased heat activation.
source: Increased temperatures synergize with PregS in activating wild-type TRPM3 (Vriens et al., 2011), see also Figure 1—figure supplement 3B, therefore it is possible that the increased PregS sensitivity of the P1090/1090Q mutant is secondary to its increased heat activation.
evidence: Speculation based on the synergy between temperature and PregS
